item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
522
ABPZ20 KNHC 061711
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Tue Oct 6 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Rachel, located several hundred miles west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico (EP92):
A broad area of low pressure located offshore of southern Mexico is
producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Environmental
conditions appear favorable for gradual development, and a tropical
depression is likely to form within the next day or so while the
system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward. Regardless
of development, heavy rainfall is expected across portions of
southern and southwestern Mexico over the next few days. Interests
along the coast of southwestern Mexico should monitor the progress
of this system.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

South of Guatemala:
An area of low pressure is expected to form south of the coast of
Guatemala early next week. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for some gradual development of this system thereafter while it
moves generally west-northwestward around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Oct 06 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 062030
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  39
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM PDT Tue Oct 06 2026
 
...RACHEL SLIGHTLY WEAKER...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.5N 120.1W
ABOUT 675 MI...1085 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...80 MPH...130 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...979 MB...28.91 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located 
near latitude 20.5 North, longitude 120.1 West. Rachel is moving 
toward the west near 7 mph (11 km/h) A westward to 
west-northwestward motion is expected during the next few days, with 
a sharp northeastward turn late this week.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 80 mph (130 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Gradual to steady weakening is forecast the next few days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 979 mb (28.91 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 39
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Oct 06 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 062031
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  39
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 PM PDT Tue Oct 06 2026
 
Rachel continues to be impacted by northeasterly wind shear and dry 
mid-level air. Recent satellite imagery shows that the northern 
portion of the circulation is eroding, with the eye now open on the 
northern side. Cloud-top temperatures have warmed, and deep 
convection is now primarily confined to the southern semicircle. The 
latest satellite intensity estimates range between 73 and 85 kt. 
Given the degraded satellite appearance, the initial intensity is 
lowered to 70 kt for this advisory.
 
The initial motion is westward, or 275/6 kt. Rachel is being steered 
west-northwestward by a subtropical ridge located over the western 
United States, and this general motion is expected to continue over 
the next couple of days. Thereafter, a mid- to upper-level trough is 
forecast to approach the U.S. West Coast, which will erode the 
western portion of the ridge. This should cause Rachel to slow down, 
turn sharply toward the northeast, and then re-accelerate. The 
latest NHC track forecast lies very close to the previous official 
forecast, though it has been nudged slightly right and faster at the 
end of the period which trends towards the HCCA and GDMI track aids.
 
Dry air entrainment is steadily eroding the convection, and the 
surrounding air mass is forecast to remain dry and stable. Although 
wind shear may briefly relax, the cyclone will soon be traversing 
cooler sea surface temperatures. Given the combination of these 
hostile environmental conditions, a steady weakening trend is 
anticipated. Convection is expected to become increasingly 
intermittent and disorganized, and the system is forecast to become 
a post-tropical cyclone by day 4. The official NHC intensity 
forecast is very similar to the previous, showing gradual then 
steady weakening throughout the forecast period.
